delete zeta-specific hypotheses from the Mellin-localizer argument
extract a finite-spectrum and function-field control theorem
compile the tail-localized inertia calculation into an exact checker

route_delta: The proof does more than establish an index-one RH criterion: it isolates a general signature-transfer mechanism from a J-invariant discrete spectrum to an admissible interpolation space.  The same route may count any finite collection of off-line J-pairs, while Bombieri supplies the finite-matrix antecedent and Connes--Consani supplies the global localizers.

seeds.title: Global J-pair signature transfer
seeds.exact_seed: For a discrete J-invariant weighted spectrum with finite fourth-distance tails and an admissible one-point interpolation family, every finite collection of r disjoint negative J-pairs produces an r-dimensional negative-definite subspace of the associated Hermitian form.
seeds.evidence: R0006 is the r=2 instance; its proof uses separate one-anchor localizers, l2 tail control, and stability of matrix inertia, none of which is specific to two pairs.
seeds.cheap_test: Write the r by r ideal block and prove an operator-norm perturbation bound from the individual l2 localizer errors; test r=1 through 8 on synthetic J-spectra.
seeds.kill_condition: A cross-term or admissibility constraint grows with r in a way that prevents simultaneous localization even for a fixed finite r.

seeds.title: Finite-spectrum index formula
seeds.exact_seed: For a finite J-invariant multiset, compute the inertia of the Weil-type pairing exactly from the fixed points and two-cycles of J, including multiplicities, and show how the pole-moment quotient changes the count by at most one.
seeds.evidence: Bombieri's finite-zero theorem gives the closest established signature count; the repository's pole form has rank two and positive index at most one.
seeds.cheap_test: Derive the block diagonal form symbolically and verify every orbit type by exact rational matrices before formalizing the linear-algebra statement.
seeds.kill_condition: The proposed count is already exactly Bombieri's theorem after notation alignment, leaving only a documentation/formalization task.

seeds.title: Certified spectral-inertia checker
seeds.exact_seed: Given algebraic or interval-enclosed spectral points, multiplicities, a J-action, localizer evaluations, and certified l2 tail bounds, emit a rational interval matrix whose inertia proves the corresponding finite-index lower bound.
seeds.evidence: The proof obligation reduces to a small Hermitian perturbation inequality after the analytic localizer and tail certificates are supplied.
seeds.cheap_test: Implement a two-pair checker with exact rational balls and reproduce the R0006 -2m identity on synthetic spectra and the finite function-field analogue.
seeds.kill_condition: The required localizer/tail data cannot be represented by independently checkable finite intervals, so the program merely reasserts the analytic theorem.

seeds.title: Index-one criterion as a prior-art synthesis
seeds.exact_seed: Determine whether R0006 is an unstated corollary obtained by combining Bombieri's negative-index count with the Connes--Consani global interpolation lemma, rather than a separately publishable theorem mechanism.
seeds.evidence: The independent audit found both ingredients and no exact index-one wording; the mathematical proof is short once they are juxtaposed.
seeds.cheap_test: Compare hypotheses and conclusions theorem-by-theorem with Bombieri Sections 8--11, Yoshida, and Connes--Consani Appendix C; ask whether the pole-moment rank argument appears explicitly.
seeds.kill_condition: An existing theorem states the identical infinite-dimensional index criterion under the same admissible test class.

conclusion: The highest-value residue is the general finite-r J-pair signature-transfer lemma, because it converts one RH corollary into a reusable spectral-index theorem and an exact certificate interface.  Novelty should remain conservative until the Bombieri--Connes--Consani composition is exhaustively compared.
